reasons: Cited clauses substantively meet the preferred position: 19.1 gives a professional-and-workmanlike standard plus material conformity to documentation/specifications; 19.2 gives ninety days for Deliverables (from the later of delivery or acceptance) and full-subscription-term conformity for hosted Services; 19.4 provides re-perform/repair/replace plus refund of Fees paid on failure to cure; 19.3 adds malicious-code and Applicable Law warranties.

The disclaimer in 19.5 is limited to implied warranties and expressly does not limit express warranties, service levels, indemnities or stated remedies, so it does not swallow the express warranty and walk-away 'AS IS' territory is not implicated.

The failed deterministic period check is a phrasing artifact only — the document writes 'ninety days' rather than '90' or 'ninety (90)' — and does not indicate a substantive shortfall below the 90-day threshold.

Consistent with the compliant claim, no redline or counterparty comment is proposed; retaining this as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue is correct. The rationale's characterization of the term-long hosted warranty as 'exceeding' 12 months is a mild overstatement but immaterial to the classification.
